Agent Name: Coder
Step Number: 1
Reason for Mistake: The Coder made a fundamental error in data interpretation and logic. Instead of looking up the specific absolute numbers of men and women with tertiary education from the census (which was the primary goal), the Coder relied on estimated percentages (21.5% and 29.3%) and an assumed total population to generate a hypothetical scenario. More critically, the Coder failed to account for the actual gender distribution of the population in 2011 Bulgaria. By assuming a 50/50 gender split (50% male, 50% female), the Coder calculated the difference based on a false premise. In reality, the male population in Bulgaria is significantly lower than the female population (roughly 44% male vs 56% female in 2011). This assumption artificially inflated the number of men and deflated the number of women relative to reality, leading to an incorrect difference. The correct approach required finding the actual counts or applying the percentages to the actual gender-specific population counts, not a generic 50/50 split.
